questions.question: What is the key difference between an operational rule and an aspirational rule?
options: Operational rules are for developers; aspirational rules are for users
Operational rules can be checked at runtime by the workbench; aspirational rules like 'be careful' have no machine-checkable test
Operational rules are written in code; aspirational rules are written in English
Operational rules are enforced automatically; aspirational rules require human review
questions.explanation: Operational rules have a named check function that the workbench can run to verify compliance. Aspirational rules ('be careful', 'test thoroughly') cannot be verified — either upgrade them to operational rules or delete them.

questions.question: What are the five rule categories in the lessons' framework?
options: Required, Optional, Forbidden, Conditional, Exception
Startup, Forbidden, Definition of done, Uncertainty handling, Approval boundaries
Security, Performance, Quality, Documentation, Testing
Pre-run, During-run, Post-run, Error-handling, Recovery
questions.explanation: The five categories: Startup (what must be true before work begins), Forbidden (what must never happen), Definition of done (what proves the task is complete), Uncertainty (what to do when unsure), and Approval (what requires human sign-off).

questions.question: What is the 'rule expiry' pattern and what problem does it solve?
options: Rules that delete themselves after a certain time to keep the workbench clean
Each rule carries an expires_at date; rules with zero violations for 60+ days trigger a warning; prevents silent rule rot and overloaded rule sets
A system for automatically updating rules when requirements change
A way to temporarily disable rules during deployments
questions.explanation: Rule expiry: each rule carries an expires_at (default 90 days). After 60 days without a violation, the checker warns and the next quarterly review decides to keep, weaken to info, or delete. Without expiry, Cloudflare's data shows rule sets grow to 80+ rules with most never firing.

questions.question: What is the 'markdown-as-source, JSON-as-cache' pattern for rule management?
options: Store rules in markdown for humans to read, and in JSON for programmatic access, keeping both in sync manually
agent-rules.md is the authored file; agent-rules.lock.json is a cache regenerated by pre-commit hook — markdown diffs are reviewable, JSON parsing stays out of hot path
Convert markdown rules to JSON at deployment time
Use JSON as the source and generate markdown documentation automatically
questions.explanation: The pattern: agent-rules.md is the human-authored source (readable in code review diffs), agent-rules.lock.json is a cache generated by pre-commit hook for fast runtime parsing. Same shape as package.json/package-lock.json and Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock.

questions.question: How do framework guardrails relate to the rule set defined in this lesson?
options: They are alternatives; use one or the other but not both
The rule set is the human-readable reviewable contract; framework guardrails (OpenAI SDK guardrails, LangGraph interrupts) are the runtime enforcement that implements it
Framework guardrails replace the need for a rule set
The rule set is for development; framework guardrails are for production
questions.explanation: The rule set is the human-readable, version-controlled contract that defines what should be enforced. Framework guardrails (OpenAI Agents SDK guardrails, LangGraph interrupts) implement those rules at runtime. You need both: runtime catches violations, the rule set proves the runtime is doing the right thing.

questions.question: Where should a rule that doesn't fit any of the five categories go?
options: Into an 'Other' catch-all category
A rule that does not fit one of the five usually wants to be split into two rules; force the split
Into a separate miscellaneous rules file
Delete it, because if it cannot be categorized it is not important
questions.explanation: If a rule doesn't fit cleanly into one of the five categories (Startup, Forbidden, Definition of done, Uncertainty, Approval), it usually wants to be two separate rules. Force the split — it clarifies intent and makes each check more specific.
